text:
maria.g: quick heads-up — found a repro where rotary-phase scaling + 8bit quant on the new llama-variant causes token bleed across cached prefixes. small sample attached.

ken.t: ugh. can you paste the minimal repro here? is this prefill vs incremental decode mismatch?

maria.g: minimal steps: 1) load quantized model q8_0 with rotary_scale=0.5 2) prefill with long prompt (~6k tokens) 3) generate with incremental KV reuse. output shows words from the prefix reappearing in wrong positions after wrap.

andy: can you share the exact rotary config? we changed default scaling last week. also which kernel (cuda/cudnn/faster-attn) you running?

maria.g: rotary_scale: 0.5, use_fast_kernels: true (ephemeral canary build), compile flags: "--enable-rope-scale --prefer-fused-attn"

robin: any chance this is the phase-wrap edge at sequence boundary? i've seen similar when position ids are offset by cache stitching.

maria.g: that's my suspicion — looks like when KV cache length crosses a power-of-two boundary the rotary phase multiplies wrong. reproduce snippet (truncated):

```
PROMPT: "The history: Alice went to the market. She saw a red bicycle."
GENERATE 1: after 350 tokens of history -> "...market. She saw a red bicycle. bicycle was shining..."  <-- repeat
```

ken.t: interesting. does this happen on fp16 too or only quant?

maria.g: fp16 seems fine. suspect quantized rotary amplitude underflow combined with integer index wrap.

eval-bot: ran baseline evals v9 on q8_0 with rotary_scale=0.5 — 3/50 prompts showed prefix-duplication consistent with report.

andy: can you bisect between old runtime (no rope-scaling) and current? if it's only the scaling path we can fast revert.

maria.g: will run bisect now. quick note: reproduced at ctx=8192 and 16384; not at 4096. so not strictly linear by length.

robin: that suggests an indexing window / stripe width effect. maybe floor(div(pos, stripe)) applied incorrectly when quant rounding occurs.

ken.t: log we need: (1) saved kv key/val tensors before and after the boundary (hex dump ok), (2) computed rotary phasors for affected positions, (3) sample detokenized output and token ids.

maria.g: putting logs in /tmp/rotphase-repro-1862345678.tar.gz and will upload to the infra run. sharing link: https://internal.s3/rotphase-repro-1862345678.tar.gz

andy: thanks. i'll run a quick compare on the kernel math with and without quant cast. if we can reproduce with small seq length we can write a unit test.

maria.g: FYI adding a temporary mitigation: when position crosses stripe boundary, force re-eval of rotary cos/sin with float-accum then cast back. reduces perf but stops bleed. test patch: 

```python
# naive mitigation
phasor = compute_phasor_float(pos)
phasor = quantize(phasor)
apply_rotary(kv, phasor)
```

robin: ok to try as short-term. open a PR and mark as experimental flag. add perf regression note.

ken.t: also check our prefix-eviction logic — if we evict and then re-prefill, offset mapping must remain consistent. might be interaction with prefix caching.

maria.g: filed issue: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/ML-ROT-234. attaching repro steps and logs in the ticket.

eval-bot: scheduled nightly regression job to run the repro on dedicated pooled GPUs with 8bit and fp16 variants. will post results in-thread tomorrow. :robot_face: 

maria.g: thanks all — i'll ping when bisect results are up. :thumbsup:
